why: Chosen by the human (2026-10-15) after exp09 map_v1/parts_v1: does an in-context second step move a bound bridge out of the J-space (family L)?

items.per_family: 80, a seeded sample (seed 0) of the eligible items

eligibility: B, C and O each change one token against the original (token-aligned), and the greedy continuations' first answer word of the set (R, B: the capitals; L: the colours) is the bridge's (B, O) and X's (C)

counterfactuals.C: the bridge set to X, every country still in the prompt. R: the city replaced by the first city of X, in a seeded order (9000 + index), whose prompt lines up token for token; B: the queried person and X's holder swap countries; L: as B
counterfactuals.O: X's and Z's holders swap countries (off the path; the answer stays)

groups.question: the question's tokens after C's changed ones (R: after the city; B: the whole question)
groups.cue: the cue phrase, from the cue word to the word before the final ' is' (the swaps' positions)

outcome: the patched greedy continuation's first capital of the set: X's capital (b), the bridge's (A), other
generation: greedy, 8 new tokens, an item's runs batched 32 at a time (Model.generate_batch: equal to single runs up to batched-kernel rounding, which changed only degenerate continuations in a check)
question: At each family's window, which part of the copy carries the bridge: its J-space part or the rest?
eligibility_from: the map run's items.jsonl (the same items and seeded sample, not regenerated)

parts.full: δ = h_C - h_B at the question group
parts.lens2: δ's projection on span{v_I, v_X}, J++'s unit vectors of the two countries; not_lens2 the rest
parts.jspace: δ's 25-atom signed OMP part over J++'s unit letter-token vectors; not_jspace the rest

controls: each part along a seeded random direction at the same per-position norm; O's full copy

decision.step_score: per item, the share of window layers at which the copy gives X's capital; paired bootstraps
decision.parts: per family, exp04's rule: outside if not_jspace - jspace is above 0 and jspace - its null is not; inside if jspace - not_jspace is above 0 and not_jspace - its null is not; otherwise both or neither (the same for lens2)
decision.hypothesis: supported if R is 'inside' or 'both or neither' with jspace above its null, and B is 'outside'; refuted if B's jspace is above its null; a family with an empty window is not interpreted
decision.L: bind_lookup only: L 'outside' (as brew): an in-context second step moves the bound bridge out of the J-space; L 'inside' (as B): it does not, so brew's difference is its first step (a table lookup) or its format; otherwise inconclusive
